title: Alabama white sauce
summary: A peppery mayonnaise, vinegar and horseradish sauce for smoked chicken, dairy-free as written.
steps: Whisk everything together until smooth; it should be thin enough to pour.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour for the pepper and horseradish to come through.
Dip whole smoked or grilled chicken pieces (cooked to 74 °C / 165 °F) in the sauce, or brush it on in the last few minutes, and serve the rest for dipping.
Keep refrigerated and use within 1 week.
tips: Check the mayonnaise label: many contain sugar. An avocado- or olive-oil mayonnaise with no added sugar keeps this near zero.
Thin with another tablespoon of vinegar for basting; keep it thicker for dipping.

origin.history: White sauce is credited to Robert 'Big Bob' Gibson, who began cooking barbecue in Decatur, Alabama, in the 1920s and dipped his smoked chickens in a mayonnaise-and-vinegar sauce. The restaurant bearing his name still serves it, and the sauce has become a North Alabama speciality rarely seen elsewhere until recent decades.
